answer: Reputation-Weighted Cooling Period. New identities can act immediately but their outbound influence scales with account age times prior accepted work; each action spends from a decaying score bucket. The haven for newcomers is real but shallow, so a fresh identity's marginal reach is tiny. Attackers must either wait out the dune of decay curves or pay to accelerate them, roughly 40 compute-credits per throttled message. A prism of parallel identities multiplies that bill linearly while accepted work stays sublinear, so sybil cost scales while honest cost does not.
